repo.description: GitHub repository in owner/repo format (e.g. acme/api-service)

issue_number.description: The GitHub issue number to triage

fetch_issue.description: Fetch the issue details from GitHub

triage_issue.description: Classify the issue severity and draft a triage comment. Pauses for human approval — the agent's output (severity, labels, comment_draft) is displayed to the reviewer before any writes reach GitHub.
triage_issue.prompt:
Triage GitHub issue #{{ run.params.issue_number }} in {{ run.params.repo }}.

ISSUE
Title: {{ context.resources.fetch_issue.title }}
Body:
{{ context.resources.fetch_issue.body }}

Produce a triage output for the engineering team:
- severity: one of critical, high, medium, low
  (critical = service down or data loss; high = significant degradation;
  medium = user-impacting bug without outage; low = minor or no user impact)
- labels: array of label strings for issue type and priority (e.g. ["bug", "P1", "memory-leak"])
- comment_draft: a concise internal triage note — not a customer reply
  - One sentence stating the assessed severity and reason
  - 2–3 concrete next steps for the responding engineer
  - No greetings, no "thank you for reporting", no customer-facing language; under 150 words

resolution_messages.approve: Approved — comment and labels will be posted to GitHub.
resolution_messages.reject: Rejected — no writes posted to GitHub.

post_comment.description: Post the approved triage comment on the GitHub issue

apply_labels.description: Apply the triage labels to the GitHub issue
